process_area.title: OCM Strategy, Governance & Change Readiness Assessment

value_stream.name: Organizational Change Management, Digital Adoption & Transformation Enablement

fields.Participants: CEO, CHRO (links to VS-103), PMO (VS-112), Innovation/Digital (VS-30), OpEx (VS-133), Communications (VS-14.3/VS-103.1)
fields.Trigger: Program stand-up; transformation portfolio established; annual review
fields.Volume: Enterprise OCM function (5 entities, ~6,762 employees, 200 stores)

workflows.name: OCM Strategy, Operating Model & Transformation Governance

Automation Opportunity: - Change-readiness criteria embedded in project stage-gates; transformation-portfolio dashboard
Controls: - CTL-632: change-readiness gate before go-live; transformation-board oversight
Cross-references: - links to VS-112 (PMO), VS-133 (OpEx), VS-30 (digital), VS-103 (HR), VS-36 (governance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **No-owner risk**: Change happens *to* people with no owner of the people-side; mitigated by chartered CoE
- **Fragmentation risk**: Every project invents its own change approach; mitigated by enterprise taxonomy and governance
System Touchpoints: - Transformation/PMO platform (links to VS-112); governance (VS-36); HR (VS-103); comms (VS-103.1)

steps.activity: CHRO define the OCM operating model: a central CoE with embedded change leads on major programs; the relationship to the PMO (VS-112), OpEx (VS-133), HR (VS-103), and Comms (VS-14.3); and the enterprise change taxonomy
CHRO author the change governance: the transformation board, decision rights, stage-gates that include change-readiness criteria, and benefit-realization linkage (VS-112/VS-133)
CEO/Board ratify and cascade; integrate change-readiness reporting into governance (VS-36)

fields.Participants: PMO (VS-112), function VPs, HR workforce planning (VS-103.3), OpEx (VS-133)
fields.Trigger: Portfolio intake; capacity strain; quarterly planning
fields.Volume: Enterprise change portfolio (ERP, omnichannel, remodels VS-109, net-zero VS-108, statutory, process improvements VS-133)

Automation Opportunity: - Audience-level change-load analytics; auto-detection of overlapping impacts
Controls: - CTL-632 (ensure controlled execution — OCM Strategy, Governance & Change Readiness Assessment (PA-134.1).)
- CTL-632: change-window policy; transformation-board sequencing approval
Cross-references: - links to VS-112 (PMO), VS-103.3 (workforce), VS-07 (store ops/seasons), VS-109 (remodels)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Saturation risk**: Too many changes at once → adoption collapse; mitigated by capacity planning and sequencing
- **Trade-disruption risk**: Changes deployed during peak harm sales; mitigated by change-windows aligned to retail calendar (VS-07)
System Touchpoints: - Portfolio/PMO platform (VS-112); workforce planning (VS-103.3); audience-impact map (W4076)

steps.activity: CHRO/PMO maintain the enterprise change portfolio (every initiative changing how people work), assess cumulative change load by audience (store/DC/HQ/function), and identify saturation/overload
CHRO lead prioritization and sequencing: sequence to absorb capacity, de-conflict simultaneous impacts on the same audience, and protect frontline trading (peak seasons links to VS-07)
CHRO report change load and capacity to the transformation board, and recommend defer/accelerate/combine decisions

fields.Volume: Per major initiative (audiences: executives, store managers, associates, DC staff, vendors, B2B customers)

Controls: - CTL-632 (ensure controlled execution — OCM Strategy, Governance & Change Readiness Assessment (PA-134.1).)
- CTL-632: engagement plan approved by sponsor; segment coverage validated
Cross-references: - links to VS-14.3 (comms), VS-103 (HR), VS-107 (key accounts for B2B stakeholders)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Blind-spot risk**: Missing a key influencer; mitigated by structured mapping and manager input
- **One-size risk**: Generic comms that miss segment needs; mitigated by segmentation

steps.activity: OCM map stakeholders (influence × interest), identify champions/resistors/key-influencers, and segment audiences by impact and readiness
OCM build the engagement plan per segment (what they need to know/feel/do, channel, cadence, owner) and align to comms (VS-14.3)
OCM validate with sponsors/managers, refine through the change, and feed insights to resistance management (W4085)

fields.Participants: Initiative team, affected process owners, HR role design (VS-102.1), OpEx (VS-133)
fields.Volume: Per major initiative (process, role, system, KPI, location impacts)

Automation Opportunity: - Impact-assessment templating; affected-people auto-count from HR master (VS-29 MDM-011)
Controls: - CTL-632 (ensure controlled execution — OCM Strategy, Governance & Change Readiness Assessment (PA-134.1).)
- CTL-632: impact assessment reviewed by HR and process owner; role changes via job architecture
Cross-references: - links to VS-102.1 (job architecture), VS-133 W4050 (process), VS-19.4 (training)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Underestimate risk**: Impact seen as small when it's big for affected roles; mitigated by role-level analysis
- **Role-ambiguity risk**: New process without clear role design; mitigated by job-architecture linkage (VS-102.1)
System Touchpoints: - Process architecture (links to VS-133 W4050); job architecture (VS-102.1); HR (VS-103); training/LMS (VS-19.4)

steps.activity: OCM/process owner assess impacts: which processes (W4050), roles, systems, KPIs, locations, and behaviors change, and the magnitude (incremental vs transformational)
OCM/HR quantify affected people by role/location (e.g., 200 store managers, ~5,800 associates, 600 DC staff), and identify role/job-design changes (links to VS-102.1)
OCM translate impacts into the training/enablement plan (W4090), comms plan (W4081), and resistance-focus (W4085)

Automation Opportunity: - Readiness dashboard; pulse-analytics with trend detection
Controls: - CTL-632 (ensure controlled execution — OCM Strategy, Governance & Change Readiness Assessment (PA-134.1).)
- CTL-632: readiness gate criteria; documented go/no-go decision
Pain Points / Risks: - **Go-when-not-ready risk**: Launching into an unready organization; mitigated by readiness gate
- **Survey-fatigue risk**: Over-surveying; mitigated by coordinated enterprise pulse
System Touchpoints: - Survey/engagement platform (links to VS-103.2); people analytics (VS-103.3); change portfolio (W4074)

steps.activity: OCM/HR assess readiness: leadership alignment, past-change fatigue, capacity (W4074), capability gaps, and culture (risk appetite, trust, psychological safety)
OCM identify readiness risks and required pre-conditions (training, comms, sponsor action, quick wins), and feed the go/no-go readiness gate (W4073)
OCM/HR track culture/readiness over time (annual pulse) and link to EX (VS-103.2) and engagement

fields.Participants: Risk (VS-21.2), sponsor, process owner, BCP (VS-26), Audit (VS-21)

Automation Opportunity: - Risk-register integration; go-live readiness checklist automation
Controls: - CTL-632: rollback plan for critical changes; BCP alignment (VS-26)
Pain Points / Risks: - **No-rollback risk**: Change that can't be reversed if it fails; mitigated by rollback design and dual-running
- **Productivity-dip risk**: Post-go-live performance drop; mitigated by hypercare (W4087) and staffing buffer
System Touchpoints: - Risk register (links to VS-21.2); BCP (VS-26); change portfolio (W4074); audit (VS-21)

steps.activity: OCM/Risk identify change-specific risks: adoption failure, productivity dip, customer/service disruption, compliance lapse during transition, key-person dependency, and reversal/reputational risk
OCM build mitigation: phasing, rollback plan, hypercare (W4087), backup/BCP (VS-26), dual-running where critical, and contingency comms
OCM monitor risks through go-live, escalate per the risk framework (VS-21.2), and capture lessons (W4096)

fields.Participants: Executive sponsors, CEO, CHRO, Transformation Board
fields.Volume: Per major initiative (executive sponsor per transformation)

Controls: - CTL-632 (ensure controlled execution — OCM Strategy, Governance & Change Readiness Assessment (PA-134.1).)
- CTL-632: named, accountable sponsor; sponsor actions logged
Pain Points / Risks: - **Absent-sponsor risk**: Sponsor in name only; mitigated by activation and visibility measurement
- **Mixed-signal risk**: Sponsors contradicting the change; mitigated by sponsor alignment

steps.activity: CHRO ensure every major initiative has an accountable, visible executive sponsor, and brief the sponsor on their role (vision, remove barriers, visible commitment, model the change)
CHRO equip sponsors with talking points, comms cadence, and visible actions (store/DC visits, town halls links to VS-103.1), and align sponsors across initiatives to avoid mixed signals
CHRO measure sponsor effectiveness (sponsor-visibility feedback) and address gaps

fields.Trigger: Demand on the OCM function; partner engagement
fields.Volume: Enterprise OCM capability + external OCM partners/consultants

Controls: - CTL-632 (ensure controlled execution — OCM Strategy, Governance & Change Readiness Assessment (PA-134.1).)
- CTL-632: partner due diligence (links to VS-34); knowledge-transfer criteria for exit
Cross-references: - links to VS-34 (procurement), VS-103 (HR), VS-135 (TBM), VS-19.4 (L&D)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Capacity-shortfall risk**: Demand exceeds OCM capacity; mitigated by capacity planning and partners
- **Dependency risk**: Over-reliance on consultants; mitigated by knowledge transfer and internal build

steps.activity: CHRO plan OCM capacity vs demand (portfolio W4074), build internal OCM competency (certifications, playbooks), and integrate with HR capability (VS-103/VS-19.4)
CHRO/Procurement engage external OCM partners where capacity/specialty requires (ERP OCM, large transformations), with due diligence and SOWs (links to VS-34)
CHRO manage partner performance, knowledge transfer (avoid dependency), and report spend/value (links to VS-135 TBM)
